findings.now: So during this protocol, do not trust your social intuition: assume you are misreading every room, at least until your heart rate is back down to your usual resting rate, and under 90 BPM, since a racing heart means your reasoning brain is offline (see the "Metabolic Red Line" below).
findings.published: Rule: During this protocol, do not trust your social intuition. It is calibrated to “Threat,” not “Truth.”
findings.why: NOW drops the stated reason for the rule (your intuition is calibrated to "Threat," not "Truth") and the "Rule:" label, so the instruction reads as a consequence of the previous sentence instead of a named rule with its own reason.
where: A Complete Guide to Bio-De-Armoring (the Cognitive Warning, as it would read), P2

findings.now: So during this protocol, do not trust your social intuition: assume you are misreading every room, at least until your heart rate is back down to your usual resting rate, and under 90 BPM, since a racing heart means your reasoning brain is offline (see the "Metabolic Red Line" below).
findings.published: Assume you are misreading every room until your heart rate is below 90 BPM.
findings.why: The one plain threshold (below 90 BPM) has become two conditions joined by ", and" behind an "at least", so a reader has to reread to work out whether they need their own resting rate, under 90, or both, and whether the rule ends even then; the added "reasoning brain is offline" clause, which isn't explained here, makes the sentence longer still.
where: A Complete Guide to Bio-De-Armoring (the Cognitive Warning, as it would read), P2
